profile.headline: Java Full Stack Developer (ReactJS, Spring, AWS)
profile.summary: Eric is infatuated with all aspects of Web Development, as such Eric is always working on personal projects to deepen his knowledge as a full stack developer.  Eric believes in mastering the fundamentals behind web development: HTML, CSS, Javascript, the DOM, HTTP, and OOP.  He also likes studying programming languages in general with his favorite begin Java.  In addition to Java, Eric also knows Ruby, Javascript, SQL, and has a particular fondness for software testing.  Eric hopes to one day to give back to the software community by mentoring others in software development.

positions.title: Layoff/position eliminated
positions.description: Laid off due to government shutdown, was a sub-contractor doing Quality Assurance for State Department software at the time.  Looking for opportunities in Software Development, also open to any positions in the Defense Industry.

positions.title: Software Test Engineer
positions.description: Part of a team of Test Engineers running manual tests on a system which audits the Passport applications submitted to the State Department, moved onto manual testing of State Departments Crisis Management System.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Working for Cinteot in a subcontractor role under Peraton as the primary contractor.  The account is with the US State Department and its Consular Systems Modernization (CSM) program.  Wrote Unit Tests for the Online Passport Renewal (OPR) ReactJS based front end.  Test coverage tools required both component and their associated hooks to be at 80% or greater.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Research into highly valued programming skill sets in the DC Metro area, with end result leading to detailed study on Javascript/React and Java/Spring/Maven.  At the end of this period concluded with job search and technical interview preparation.

company.name: Area Specific Skill Acquisition and Job Search

positions.title: Full Time Student
positions.description: Started Launch School as a full time student in April of 2018.  Launch School is an online web development school dedicated to mastery based learning and a focus on the fundamentals of both web development and programming.  Thorough instruction and assessments on Object Oriented Programming (with Ruby as the language), problem solving techniques, basics of Objected Oriented design, database interaction using SQL, HTML, CSS, essentials of the HTTP protocol, the Javascript programming language, program solving and program design using Javascript (much like was what was done with Ruby), the DOM API, AJAX, and some exposure to REST API design.  Throughout the course of instruction, applications were built with the above technologies only using web development libraries when a full stack application was required (Sinatra for Ruby and Express for Javascript).  Since Launch School emphasis was always on the fundamentals, the student learned just enough about the web development library to get the application working.  January through March were used to prepare and move to the DC area.

positions.title: Full Stack Web Developer
positions.description: Worked as a contractor for a team which maintains ticket escalation software at AT&T.  The team is part of a larger ongoing effort (GCSBizOps) by AT&T to further automate the process of responding to network outages or other network related issues.  Setup and successfully ran end to end tests on the ticket escalation softwares using Nightwatch.js.  Documented the process which was eventually adopted by other teams in GCSBizOps.  Updated large segment of code to generate contact information for those following an escalated ticket, began the process of unit testing the Javascript/Bootstrap/jQuery front end code base with Mocha/Chai/JSDOM.  Introduced a simple Object Relational Mapper class to abstract away the Perl::DBI interface from the most common queries to the database.  I was laid-off for no concrete reason.  Shockingly, this happened four months after I was promoted to a Mid Range Developer.

company.name: Continue to Retrain as a Software Developer

positions.title: Aspiring Web Developer
positions.description:
Met 3-4 times a month with an experienced Ruby on Rails developer who kindly volunteered to mentor me.

Didi full stack development work for a home school sports league website.  Got Parental sign up, log in, child registration, and sports sign up to work.  Used my own authentication code, based on the Michael Hartl Ruby on Rails tutorial.  Front end styling was done with Bootstrap and back end testing with Rspec/Capybara.  Coded in Rails 4.

positions.title: Aspiring Web Developer
positions.description: My parents were in dire need of help with their estate, so I temporarily moved in with them and cleared the way for a clean transition to their final home.  During this time heavy review work was done on Ruby and Ruby on Rails via the Pragmatic Studio (Beginning Ruby, Rails I, and Rails II) along with the Michael Hartl tutorial on Rails.

positions.locationName: RoleModel Software 6720 Rolemodel Way,  Holly Springs, NC 27540

positions.title: Apprentice Developer
positions.description:
Assigned to work on a custom graphics project using HTML5 Canvas and Javascript.  The project was for Decks.com and the end goal was to produce software which would allow customers to design their own custom deck with rendered 2D and 3D views along with a permit plan and a material list.

I was initially assigned to work on the cap rails for project along with picket implementation.  All software was written in pure Javascript and model testing used the Jasmine testing framework.  Any templating used Jade.

The cap rail work was very challenging as the cap rails had to be cut properly depending on the number of posts required to support the deck and also on whether the deck was rectangular, octagonal, or a hybrid shape.  Stairs were a real challenge as both the pickets and posts had to be cut at an angle equal to the stair angle.  The cap rails then had to lay properly on the top edge of the angled posts and pickets.

I also contributed to some joist work which were used to support the deck frame.  Again the joists had to be properly cut to accommodate either rectangular, octagonal, or hybrid decks.  Multiple joists had to be implemented when the deck surpassed a certain size.

Finally, I was also responsible for the material list.  A list of properly cut wood, nails, screws, joints, and any other miscellaneous deck building material had to be generated based on any given deck design.  The wood had to be partitioned among the most favorable and least expensive cuts from the lumber yard.

positions.title: Student RoleModel Craftsmanship Academy
positions.description:
Selected as a student at the in house developer school at RoleModel Software.  The school was known as the Craftsmanship Academy.

Underwent a very rigorous and fast paced introduction to all aspects of modern software development.  Languages learned were Ruby, Javascript, and Objective-C in addition to HTML and CSS.

Lots of emphasis on Test Driven Development, Agile methodology, Data Structures, Network technology, and Version Control.

Initial project was a command line version of the War card game.  Later projects were a command line version of the Game of Fish which worked over the network, an Old Maid game using the Javascript Backbone.js Framework, and the Game of Fish using the Sinatra and Ruby on Rails Frameworks.

I was given an extra month to finish up my final project because I was significantly behind the other Academy participants.

positions.title: Aspiring software developer
positions.description:
IBM laid off the entire microprocessor development team at the Research Triangle Park in July of 2013.  The layoff was not performance related as everyone from the second line managers on down were let go.

A lot of time was spent getting our house ready to sell as this provided money for living as my wife sought to get re-employed in the legal field.

I initially worked on iOS development, learning Objective-C and was just beginning to learn the Apple SDK before an opportunity at RoleModel Software opened up.

company.name: Initial Retraining for a career in software

positions.title: VLSI Circuit Designer
positions.description:
PowerPC Embedded Processors (PEPS):
Initial development projects included flip-flop design and carry save adders for the integer multipliers of the PPC405 and the PPC440 embedded processors.  Worked with the physical designers for integration into the floorplan and worked with the logic design team to address timing closure.

Circuit multiplier lead for follow on to the PPC440.  Added Multiply-Add functionality, the design was slated to use dynamic logic to achieve timing goals.  However, the entire project was cancelled before the multiplier was finished.

Designed three graphics macros for Xbox 360 project.  Responsibilities included schematic entry, physical verification, timing closure, noise analysis, and schematic to logic entry equivalence.

Designed and implemented a four stage pipelined integer multiplier for the Power7 microprocessor.  Migrated the design to the Power7+.  Design included a 128 bit integer add in the last stage.  Responsible for all schematic entry, physical verification, electrical verification including noise immunity, and minimizing power dissipation.  The second pass of the design resulted in > 50% reduction in power dissipation while maintaining timing closure.

Designed three macros for the Instruction Sequencing Unit (ISU) on the Power7+ and Power8 microprocessors.  Same responsibilities for design as the Power7 project.  Heavy interlock with the physical designer for the ISU because of severe wiring constraints.  The designs were handed off to another engineer for maintenance and successive alterations were minimal despite major changes in the CAD tool for noise analysis.

Completed the design of two General Purpose Register Files (GPR) for the Power8 microprocessor.  Implemented schematic and layout changes reflecting altered logic of the designs.  Prepared for and had the design reviewed by the lead GPR designer for the Power8 project.  All timing, electrical, and logic equivalence requirements were met.

positions.title: Truck Loader
positions.description: Worked part time at UPS loading trucks early in the morning before the drivers left for their routes.  Attended Northern Virginia Community College part time taking classes in Electrical Engineering and Mechanical Engineering in preparation for my application to Virginia Tech.

positions.title: Staff Assistant
positions.description: Worked at a vending company during the day while in the evenings I assisted the Navigator Staff and their ministry to the Marines on Camp Pendleton, CA.  Led Bible Studies and on base evangelism.

positions.title: Junior Officer
positions.locationName: Annapolis, MD; Quantico, VA; Fort Knox, KY; Camp Pendleton, CA; Okinawa, Japan
positions.description:
Immediately after graduation from the Naval Academy assigned temporary duty training the incoming USNA freshmen ("plebes") on the use of the M1911 .45 caliber pistol.  All aspects of marksmanship and weapons safety were taught.

Attended six months of The Basic School in Quantico, VA which is required training for all USMC officers regardless of their occupational specialty.  At the end of the training I was able to select Armor (Tanks) as my occupational specialty.

Sent to Fort Knox, KY for four months of Armor Officer Basic Training.  Marine Officers are sent to Fort Knox to train along side the Army.

Tank Platoon Commander, C Company, First Tank Battalion, Camp Pendleton, CA.  Responsible for the training, performance reports, and discipline of 20 enlisted Marines along with the maintenance and deployment of five M60A1 Main Battle Tanks.  Conducted regular field training which included live fire exercises.  Tactical emphasis was a platoon operating within the context of a company level combined arms unit (mechanized infantry along with armor).  Particular attention paid to safety during live first exercises.

Oversaw the first implementation of the Battalion's Tank Commander School.  The school was an in house operation for enlisted personnel which enhanced the training of current and future tank commanders.  Initial curriculum was jointly developed with the Staff Noncommissioned in charge of the school.  Curriculum involved a significant amount of field exercises with an emphasis on perfecting the speed and precision of tank gunnery.

Executive Officer, C-Tracks, First Tank Battalion, Camp Pendleton, CA.  Based on the guidance from the commanding officer, responsible for the day to day operations of over 100 Marines and 17 tanks and one recovery vehicle.  Scheduled company wide training and ran the logistic effort during field operations.  Along with company First Sergeant ran the logistical operations for the six month deployment to Okinawa, Japan.

experience.locationName: Annapolis, MD; Quantico, VA; Fort Knox, KY; Camp Pendleton, CA; Okinawa, Japan
experience.description:
Immediately after graduation from the Naval Academy assigned temporary duty training the incoming USNA freshmen ("plebes") on the use of the M1911 .45 caliber pistol.  All aspects of marksmanship and weapons safety were taught.

Attended six months of The Basic School in Quantico, VA which is required training for all USMC officers regardless of their occupational specialty.  At the end of the training I was able to select Armor (Tanks) as my occupational specialty.

Sent to Fort Knox, KY for four months of Armor Officer Basic Training.  Marine Officers are sent to Fort Knox to train along side the Army.

Tank Platoon Commander, C Company, First Tank Battalion, Camp Pendleton, CA.  Responsible for the training, performance reports, and discipline of 20 enlisted Marines along with the maintenance and deployment of five M60A1 Main Battle Tanks.  Conducted regular field training which included live fire exercises.  Tactical emphasis was a platoon operating within the context of a company level combined arms unit (mechanized infantry along with armor).  Particular attention paid to safety during live first exercises.

Oversaw the first implementation of the Battalion's Tank Commander School.  The school was an in house operation for enlisted personnel which enhanced the training of current and future tank commanders.  Initial curriculum was jointly developed with the Staff Noncommissioned in charge of the school.  Curriculum involved a significant amount of field exercises with an emphasis on perfecting the speed and precision of tank gunnery.

Executive Officer, C-Tracks, First Tank Battalion, Camp Pendleton, CA.  Based on the guidance from the commanding officer, responsible for the day to day operations of over 100 Marines and 17 tanks and one recovery vehicle.  Scheduled company wide training and ran the logistic effort during field operations.  Along with company First Sergeant ran the logistical operations for the six month deployment to Okinawa, Japan.
